guidelines: ACOG Practice Bulletin No. 209: Primary Dysmenorrhea
assessment: Menstrual cramps (dysmenorrhea) are caused by increased prostaglandin production in the endometrium, triggering uterine muscle contractions.
lifestyleMeasures: Local heat application (heating pad or hot water bottle at ~40°C) across the lower abdomen relaxes myometrial tension with efficacy comparable to oral NSAIDs.
Gentle restorative yoga postures such as Balasana (Child's Pose), Supta Baddha Konasana, and gentle pelvic tilts.
Stay well hydrated and reduce high-sodium foods to alleviate pelvic vascular congestion.
otcGuidance: First-line pharmacological relief includes NSAIDs (e.g., ibuprofen, mefenamic acid) taken with food at symptom onset, subject to medical advice.
redFlags: Seek in-person gynecological evaluation if pain is incapacitating, resists analgesics, radiates intensely to rectum or thighs, or is accompanied by fever or abnormal foul discharge.

guidelines: International Evidence-based Guideline for PCOS Assessment (Rotterdam Criteria / Endocrine Society)
assessment: Normal menstrual cycles range between 21 and 35 days. Cycles exceeding 38 days or fewer than 9 periods per year indicate oligomenorrhea, commonly related to hormonal imbalance, chronic anovulation, PCOS, thyroid dysfunction, or hyperprolactinemia.
recommendations: Maintain a 3-to-6 month menstrual calendar tracking cycle lengths, luteal symptoms, and flow volume.
Consult a gynecologist or endocrinologist for a hormonal profile (Serum Total/Free Testosterone, LH/FSH ratio, Fasting Insulin, TSH, Prolactin, and pelvic ultrasound).
Adopt a low-glycemic, anti-inflammatory dietary pattern with regular low-impact aerobic activity to enhance insulin sensitivity.
redFlags: Absence of menses for >90 consecutive days (secondary amenorrhea) or sudden excessive abnormal bleeding requires immediate clinical evaluation.
